title: introduce-latency-indexed-provisioner-and-cost-aware-throttle
text:
introduce-latency-indexed-provisioner-and-cost-aware-throttle

description:
Motivation: We see frequent autoscaler thrash when a small subset of latency-sensitive tenants sporadically generate tail-latency spikes. The existing fleet autoscaler reacts primarily to utilization signals which causes expensive overprovisioning (especially for Dedicated customers) and oscillation across pools. This PR introduces a latency-indexed provisioner that augments utilization-based signals with a compact latency score per tenant and a lightweight contract that ranks provision priority. Additionally, a cost-aware soft-throttle is added so that tenants with low contractual priority can be gently shaped during sustained bursts instead of triggering fleet-wide scale-ups.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a new control path in the autoscaler that: 1) consumes p50/p95/p99 latency histograms emitted by the serving runtime, 2) computes a per-tenant latency index using configurable weightings and EWMA smoothing, 3) combines latency index with reserved commitment fraction and predicted token cost to produce a single provision score, 4) applies the provision score to ordering decisions when ramping capacity or selecting warmpool candidates, and 5) exposes a cost-aware throttle action that can be applied as a graceful fallback (response headers indicate throttle reason). To avoid synchronized reactions across controllers, the provisioner uses randomized jittered sampling windows and a small stochastic backoff when multiple tenants trigger changes simultaneously.

Stability and rollout: implemented feature gate (alpha) behind config flags and a gradual canary rollout in Dedicated. Added integration test harness that replays production latency traces and verifies no more than one scale-up per five-minute window for identical synthetic surges. Telemetry: new metrics and logs (listed below) and an alerting recipe for ops.

Files changed (summary): see files_changed list below. Key changes include: autoscaler/provisioner/latency_indexer.go (new), autoscaler/provisioner/score_aggregator.go (new), autoscaler/throttles/cost_throttle.go (new), autoscaler/config/provisioner_v1.yaml (config flags), runtime/metrics/emit_latency_buckets.go (minor export), docs/operators/latency-indexed-provisioner.md (operator docs), tests/integration/provisioner_replay_test.go (integration), SDKs/python/examples/latency_indexer_demo.py (example showing response header on throttle).

Commits: brief summaries are below. Review summary and CI history included after commits.

Why this is different: Existing autoscaler work focused on utilization smoothing and burst credits. This PR shifts part of the decision surface to include latency-constrained objectives so Dedicated fleets can favor safety for tail-sensitive tenants without forcing fleet-wide capacity increases. The cost-aware throttle provides a predictable, observable degradation path with explicit contract reasons rather than opaque request failures.

Related: ENG-2147 (investigation into latency-driven scale events), ENG-2199 (Dedicated customer cost-surge postmortem).

commits:
1) Add latency indexer and score aggregator (mfernandez): implement EWMA-based bucket reduction, weight configuration and basic unit tests
2) Introduce cost-aware soft throttle (mfernandez): runtime header plumbing, throttle policy, e2e tests against synthetic traces
3) Integrate provisioner into autoscaler decision loop (mfernandez): hook ordering, warmpool candidate selection, feature flag and config schema
4) Telemetry and docs (mfernandez): metrics, dashboards, operator doc, example script
5) Fix lint and race in integration test harness (follow-up commit after review feedback)

review_comments:
Anil Kapoor: Please ensure the EWMA decay constants are configurable and documented; the defaults should match production traces. Also request a test that simulates two tenants spiking simultaneously to verify the stochastic backoff prevents synchronized scaling.
Priya Desai: The throttle header format looks fine but include observability keys so the console can correlate throttles to tenant IDs and provision scores. Also, avoid exposing raw cost-per-token in headers; use a hashed reason code instead.
Luca Romano: Nit: move some helper functions from score_aggregator into a helper pkg for reuse; add comments explaining the sampling jitter strategy.

author_replies:
Maya Fernandez: Addressed EWMA as configurable parameters in autoscaler/config/provisioner_v1.yaml and added tests (integration/provisioner_replay_test.go).
Maya Fernandez: Switched throttle header to throttle-reason-code and added console correlation keys; removed raw cost exposure. See sdk/python/examples/latency_indexer_demo.py for header decoding example.
Maya Fernandez: Pulled helper funcs into autoscaler/internal/sampling_helpers.go and added doc comments and unit tests.

release_notes:
Introduce 'Latency-indexed provisioner' (alpha) and a cost-aware soft throttle. Operators can opt-in via 'provisioner.alpha.latency_index' feature gate. Adds telemetry: autoscaler.latency_index.score, autoscaler.throttle.invocations, autoscaler.throttle.reason_code. Improves Dedicated fleet stability for tail-latency sensitive workloads; initial rollout is canary-only.

notes_for_ops:
Feature is behind feature gate: set provisioner.alpha.latency_index = true to enable
Default EWMA weights are conservative; consider tuning p95 weight for workloads with heavy tail latency
Throttle reason codes are documented in docs/operators/latency-indexed-provisioner.md
Dashboards added at console/metrics/dashboards/latency_indexer_overview.json
